arms.name: Experimental (Integrated Teaching Model)
arms.description: GenAI embedded throughout the design-thinking stages with explicit tool-intervention points, workshops, group collaboration, iterative production, and process feedback (PDF pp. 10-11, Section 3.4.3 and Table 2). Analyzed people count is for questionnaires, not a confirmed count of contributors to the rated projects.

arms.name: Control (Traditional Teaching Model)
arms.description: Traditional lecturer-led instruction and case analysis, primarily independent assignments and final-outcome evaluation; GenAI used sporadically for sketch generation, style reference, or material preparation, with manual drawing and conventional digital software dominant (PDF pp. 10-11, Section 3.4.3 and Table 2). Analyzed people count is for questionnaires, not a confirmed count of contributors to the rated projects.

studies.task: Complete final group illustration-design projects during a six-week Illustration Design course, submitting final images, design statements, and process summaries for expert evaluation.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, Runway, and unspecified AIGC and emotion-analysis tools
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 7, Figure 2 (visually checked after extracting page text); PDF pp. 10-11, Section 3.4.3 and Table 2. Intervention model versions and release years are not reported.

preregistration.where: No preregistration is identified in the complete article.

estimates.outcome: Overall expert evaluation score of final project (mean of five dimensions)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Six experts with teaching and industry experience in illustration and visual communication rated anonymized final group projects, presented in randomized order, on a 100-point scale (PDF pp. 11-12, Section 3.5.1; PDF p. 20, Section 4.6). The overall project score is the mean across Creativity, Applicability, Technicality, Expressiveness, and Completeness. This broad design-performance composite is coded other, following the reconciled form; it is not a standalone overall-creativity rating.

estimates.notes: The people contributing to the rated projects are not enumerated, and project membership, team sizes, and team formation are not reported; participant counts for this analysis are therefore null. The student-level questionnaire/SEM counts cannot be substituted for project contributors. Individual students were randomized, but these observations are group projects. The article does not establish whether the tabulated means use initial independent ratings or scores after discussion to consensus (PDF pp. 12, 20-21). Higher values mean better overall design-performance scores across the combined rubric, hence higher_is is other. Means, SDs, the t-test, and Cohen’s d are transcribed exactly as printed. The paper does not specify the standardizer for d. The independent-sample test treats projects as observations and reports no participant- or class-adjusted uncertainty, so se_basis is output. No mean difference, SE, or interval has been calculated. The broad composite is coded other as in the reconciled screening form and is not eligible as a pooled primary creativity record.

estimates.notes: The people contributing to the rated projects are not enumerated, and project membership, team sizes, and team formation are not reported; participant counts for this analysis are therefore null. The student-level questionnaire/SEM counts cannot be substituted for project contributors. Individual students were randomized, but these observations are group projects. The article does not establish whether the tabulated means use initial independent ratings or scores after discussion to consensus (PDF pp. 12, 20-21). The full-sample arm comparison is reported descriptively as a higher experimental-group median. Table 13 (PDF p. 21) provides individual project means; Figure 6 (PDF p. 22) shows arm distributions without printed numerical arm summaries. No arm mean, arm SD, exact median, dimension-specific test, effect size, or uncertainty for this contrast is printed. These fields remain null: no arm summaries were averaged from project rows and no values were read off the plot. The prose describes scatter points as individual expert ratings, while the point unit is not otherwise established; no figure-derived statistics are used. Higher values indicate better performance on the specified novelty or output-quality dimension.

not_extracted.reason: Qualitative experiences, perceptions, and explanatory observations; no independently scored quantitative creative-output contrast (PDF p. 13, Section 3.5.3; PDF p. 21, Section 4.6; PDF p. 23, Section 4.7).

open_items: The number of distinct students represented by the rated group projects, project-to-student membership, team sizes, and team formation are unreported (PDF pp. 12, 20-21). Estimate-level participant counts remain null.
Participant-level outcome SDs and participant- or randomized-cluster-based uncertainty are not reported. The overall-score SDs and test are at the project level (PDF p. 20, Section 4.6).

Separate arm summaries, effect sizes, tests, and uncertainty for Creativity, Applicability, Technicality, Expressiveness, and Completeness are not printed; only project rows and unlabelled distributional summaries are available (PDF pp. 21-22, Table 13 and Figure 6).
The standardizing SD used for the reported Cohen’s d is not specified (PDF p. 20, Section 4.6).
It is unclear whether the tabulated expert means and reliability coefficients use initial independent scores or scores after discussion to consensus (PDF pp. 20-22, Section 4.6 and Tables 13-14).
The prose calls Figure 6 scatter points individual expert ratings, but the relationship between those points and the project means is not documented (PDF pp. 21-22).

Intervention model versions and release years are not reported (PDF p. 7, Figure 2; PDF pp. 10-11, intervention description). The study country is not identified: College X is anonymized, and author affiliation is not a confirmed study location (PDF pp. 1 and 9).
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-10. The complete markdown conversion was read through the references and final publisher note; no appendix or separate supplement is identified. Every cited PDF page was checked using PyMuPDF text extraction; the course-tool diagram and outcome plots were also inspected in memory. The Data Availability Statement says data are contained within the article (PDF p. 28). Both instructional arms used GenAI, so all contrasts are ai_design. Individual randomization is explicit; separate instructional classes are not randomized clusters (PDF p. 9, Section 3.4.1). Study-level analyzed people counts refer to questionnaires/SEM and do not establish the people count for rated projects (PDF pp. 15 and 20). No shared sample with another paper is reported. The overall composite remains other, Creativity is novelty, and the remaining rubric dimensions are usefulness, following the reconciled form and the rubric. Eligible dimension contrasts without printed arm statistics are retained with null statistics, rather than excluded. No unassisted post-AI creative outcome or across-person diversity outcome is reported. No derived quantities or figure-read numbers are recorded.
